_what: The forums' categories, in the order the forums list them. tools/make-forum.py writes them into netlify/cb/lib.mjs between the forum:categories markers, which is the only list the server reads. Do not hand-edit those markers; edit this and run tools/check-all.sh.
_brief: Ryan's brief, 2026-10-18: a forum after Discourse, for discussions that need to last more than the CB's day, with some of the channels from our Stoat and Discord, readable only by claimed usernames, a keep per category, and categories restricted by CB role for staff areas. The hope is that the CB and the forums together let us leave Discord and Stoat entirely.
_keep: How long a topic stays after its last post: "1 week", "3 months", "6 months" or "never". A topic with no keep of its own takes default_keep. Changing a category's keep here changes it for every topic already in it, because the date a topic goes is worked out every time it is read. A pinned topic is kept while it stays pinned. Ryan's calls, 2026-10-18: three months by default, and counted from the last post, so a living conversation never vanishes mid-discussion.
_keeps_set: Since 2026-10-28 (Ryan's ask, after the CB's channels) an administrator can set a category's keep at the desk in the Moderators' room, and every post is stamped with its category's keep when it is made, so a topic is kept for the shortest of its category's keep now and every stamp in it: a longer keep reaches only what is posted after it, a shorter one everything at once. A post from before the stamps is held to the keep this file gives its category, or to its was where it names one: was is the keep a category's topics were posted under before its keep here was lengthened without everybody who posted in it saying yes, the watering hole's week. Lengthening a keep here reaches unstamped posts and nothing posted after 2026-10-28, so it is a change for everybody who posted only with their say-so. The same day, Ryan said everybody who had posted in Announcements, Events, Show your work, Props & Gratitude and Artificial Intelligence agreed to their topics being kept for good, and Work opportunities and Discourse were empty, so those and every Interests category went to never; the watering hole went from a week to three months, with was keeping its existing topics to their week.
_roles: see: who can read the category, as CB_MODS roles (moderator, board, director, administrator); null is every claimed username. start: who can start a topic in it, as roles; null is everybody who can see it. An administrator sees and starts in every category unless it says strict, which is the Town Hall's Executive Session rule: the category's own roles are the only way in. A category somebody cannot see is never sent to them, and nothing says it exists. as: the Town Hall room a category says it is for the same people as; tools/make-forum.py holds its see and strict to that room's MOD_ROOMS and STRICT_ROOMS.
_rooms: Ryan's ask and calls, 2026-10-21: every category is a room on the CB, its channel, Be seen here, its call, Follow this room, Unreads, notifications and hosting a film, under the tag forum-<slug>, and only the people who can read the category may enter it: a claimed username, with the category's see roles. A subcategory, and every year of Meeting Minutes, is its top category's room, so all of Team Docs is one. A category's room is not in cb-rooms.json, which is public; the radio is told the rooms of the categories it may read by /cb/rooms, so nobody is named a category they cannot read.
_wiki: wiki: the roles that edit every document in the category, whoever wrote it. Ryan's call, 2026-10-19: support docs on discrete topics, as living documents that several people keep up to date, in a Wiki category that never expires, where moderators and above edit any document. A document is the post that opens a topic; replies stay their writers' own, and only their writers edit them. The name of whoever edited a document last is shown on it, so a moderator's words are never passed off as its starter's. A wiki category's keep is never, because an edit does not move a topic's clock and a page nobody replied to would otherwise go.
_parents: Ryan's ask, 2026-10-20, moving the team's documents from Google Docs: a Team Docs category for moderators and above, with Field Guide, Notes and Meeting Minutes inside it and Meeting Minutes filed by year. parent: the slug of the category a subcategory stands in, which comes earlier in this list; three levels at most. A subcategory takes its parent's group, keep, roles, strict and wiki and may not set its own, so nobody is ever sent a subcategory of a category they cannot read. topics: false makes a category a shelf, holding its subcategories and no topics of its own. years: the first year of a subcategory for every year from then to this one, newest first, which the server makes as each year begins, so nobody has to add one in January; 2024 is where the Drive's Meeting Minutes folders begin. templates: true makes a category's topics the templates offered to anybody who can read it when they start a topic, which copy the template's title and words in; a pinned topic there is its read-me and is not offered, as the Drive's templates folder has one.
_coping: Ryan's call, 2026-10-18: Coping is one of the most active channels on our Discord, so it is here for people moving over, and its topics go a week after the last post, because Discord keeps that channel for ever and that is not what it is for. Do not lengthen it to match the other categories.
_left_out: From our old Discord's channels, left for Ryan or Helen to add: body doubling and the live rooms (those are calls, which every room on the street already has), and the gallery. Pictures and files arrived in posts on 2026-10-18 (Ryan's call), so a gallery could be a category now; Show your work and Pets already take pictures.
_grantmaking: Ryan's ask, 2026-10-22, moving Notion's Grants table here rather than building Notion's databases: every grant round is a topic in Grantmaking tagged grant-round, the rounds made in Notion brought in by importTopic at the time each page was made, under the username that made it, with its Grant Type and Approvals written at the top of the post, and a Grant Round template in Templates for the next one, carrying the tag. So Grantmaking keeps its topics for good (the rounds go back to 2024, and a six-month keep would let them go at once), and is a wiki for the directors and the board, so any of them can add their name to a round's Approvals, as Notion's Approvals field let them; replies stay their writers' own. Approvals are words in the post, not a field: nothing works out who approved what, and nothing counts them.

categories.name: Announcements
categories.about: News from the people who run Stimpunks. Only moderators start a topic here; anybody can reply.

categories.name: Introductions
categories.about: Say hello, if you like, and say as much or as little as you want to. Reading along is a fine way to belong too.

categories.name: Help desk
categories.about: When something on the street, the CB or the forums does not work, or you cannot find your way.

categories.name: Wiki
categories.about: How to do things on the street, the CB and the forums, one thing to a page. Every page is a living document that our moderators keep up to date, whoever started it. Something wrong or missing? Reply on the page, or ask in the Help desk.

categories.name: The watering hole
categories.about: Chat about anything, share penguin pebbles, pass the time.

categories.name: Coping
categories.about: For the hard days, and for getting through them together. Say what is going on and be met where you are; nobody has to fix anything, and nobody has to answer. What is said here stays here.

categories.name: Events
categories.about: What is coming up, and what happened: our calls, campfires, watch-togethers and anything else worth turning up for.

categories.name: Mutual aid
categories.about: To give help and to get it. Nobody owes anybody here.

categories.name: Show your work
categories.about: What you are making, writing, learning or fixing, finished or not.

categories.name: Work opportunities
categories.about: Jobs, gigs, calls for contributors and paid chances to do the work.

categories.name: Discourse
categories.about: The news, ideas and arguments of the day, and what they mean for us. Disagree well: nobody has to win, and nobody has to take part.

categories.name: Pets
categories.about: Your animals: pictures, stories, worries and questions. Animals adopted from the street's shelters are welcome here too.

categories.name: Props & Gratitude
categories.about: Thank somebody out loud for something they did, big or small. Nobody is ranked, and nobody has to be thanked to belong.

categories.name: Infodumps
categories.about: Tell us everything about the thing you love. Long is welcome.

categories.name: Reading, watching, listening, playing
categories.about: Books, films, shows, music, podcasts and games: what you are into and what you would pass along.

categories.name: Education
categories.about: Learning, schooling, unschooling and the places in between, and what they do to the people in them.

categories.name: Science and making
categories.about: Experiments, tinkering, crafts, code and anything built with your hands or your head.

categories.name: Nature
categories.about: Plants, animals, weather, places outdoors, and the ground you are standing on.

categories.name: Artificial Intelligence
categories.about: Learning, making and knowledge gardening with generative AI, and the arguments about it.

categories.name: Operations
categories.about: The work of running Stimpunks, out in the open, with room for anybody who wants to watch and learn.

categories.name: Editorial
categories.about: What we publish and how: drafts, edits, ideas for pages and the glossary.

categories.name: Moderators
categories.about: For our moderators: anything about keeping the street and the CB a good place to be.

categories.name: Team Docs
categories.about: The team’s own documents, which used to live in Google Docs: how we do things, notes, the minutes of our meetings, and the templates they start from. For moderators and above, and every document here is any of them to keep up to date.

categories.name: Field Guide
categories.about: How we do things, one thing to a page, with screenshots in the flow of the words where they help.

categories.name: Notes
categories.about: Notes worth keeping: research, drafts, plans and ideas that are not a Field Guide page or a meeting’s minutes.

categories.name: Meeting Minutes
categories.about: The minutes of our meetings, filed by the year each meeting was held.

categories.name: Templates
categories.about: What new documents start from. Start a topic anywhere you can see this and pick one under Start from a template, which copies its title and words in for you to fill. Editing a template changes what the next topic starts from, never one already started. A pinned topic here is a read-me, not a template.

categories.name: Directors
categories.about: For our directors, as the Directors' room off the Town Hall is.

categories.name: Board
categories.about: For the board, and the directors who join its meetings, as the Board room off the Town Hall is.

categories.name: Back Office Operations
categories.about: For our moderators, the directors and the board: the paperwork, systems, filings and contracts that keep Stimpunks running behind the scenes.

categories.name: Grantmaking
categories.about: For the directors and the board: the grants we make, the requests that come in, and how they are decided. Every grant round is a topic tagged grant-round, kept for good. Start one from the Grant Round template, and any director or board member can add their name to its Approvals.

categories.name: Finance
categories.about: For the directors and the board: money in, money out, budgets, banking and the books.
